budget_items.topic: Cherry sheet education aid increases (FY27 governor's proposal vs final budget)
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair walked through increases in chapter 70, charter tuition reimbursement, smart growth school reimbursement, and school choice receiving tuition between the governor's proposed and final FY27 budgets. Charter tuition and smart growth were described as highly variable year to year, while school choice receipts have trended down over 15 years.

budget_items.topic: Total cherry sheet receipts increase, including UGGA and VBS
budget_items.what_was_said: Beyond education-coded funds, the town also saw a slight increase in unrestricted general government aid and funds for the visually impaired and elderly. The chair gave a total increase across all cherry sheet receipts.

budget_items.topic: State assessments and charges (charter and school choice sending tuition)
budget_items.what_was_said: Charter school sending tuition assessed to the town increased while school choice sending tuition decreased, producing a net extra assessment for the year, all within education.

budget_items.topic: Net additional state aid for FY27
budget_items.what_was_said: Subtracting the extra assessments from the extra receipts gives the net additional aid the town received above what the town budget was originally built on.

budget_items.topic: Transfer: maintenance of buildings to grounds contracted services
budget_items.what_was_said: A year-end transfer to cover a grounds contracted-services overage.

budget_items.topic: Transfer: maintenance salaries to maintenance overtime
budget_items.what_was_said: A small transfer to cover a maintenance overtime salary overage.

budget_items.topic: Transfer: custodian salaries
budget_items.what_was_said: Funds moved from middle and high school custodian lines to elementary and primary school custodian lines to cover salary overages.

budget_items.topic: Transfer: athletic security/athletic transportation
budget_items.what_was_said: A transfer to cover athletic event security (police detail) overage, described as coming from the athletic transportation line.

budget_items.topic: Transfer: heating charges to regular transportation
budget_items.what_was_said: Surplus heating funds were moved to cover a regular transportation overage; a member noted this was because the line had been budgeted too low, since revised for FY27.

budget_items.topic: Transfer: guidance counselor and secretary salaries
budget_items.what_was_said: Funds moved from middle school guidance counselors to high school guidance counselor and secretary lines; part attributed to extra costs from summer scheduling issues.

budget_items.topic: Transfer: high school substitute salaries
budget_items.what_was_said: A transfer to cover a high school regular substitute overage.

budget_items.topic: Transfer: high school principal/assistant principal salaries
budget_items.what_was_said: Funds moved from a middle school administrative secretary line to cover high school principal and assistant principal salary overages, described as lines budgeted too low, now corrected for FY27.

budget_items.topic: Transfer: special education positions and hospital tutoring
budget_items.what_was_said: A transfer from a high school sped resource room teacher line to hospital tutoring and several special-education paraprofessional lines across schools, attributed to a staff leave of absence.

budget_items.topic: Transfer: superintendent's dues/meetings to general supplies
budget_items.what_was_said: A transfer to cover a general supplies overage in the superintendent's budget, from unused dues/meetings funds.

budget_items.topic: Percent of budget spent this year
budget_items.what_was_said: Asked what share of the budget was spent, the business staff said expenses came in essentially at full budget, with salary figures still being finalized and expected to land close to full spend.

budget_items.topic: Prior-year budget overage (context for this year's transfers)
budget_items.what_was_said: Referencing an earlier-year budget shortfall the district had to give back, a member asked what share of the budget that represented; staff estimated it as a couple of percent of the total budget.

budget_items.topic: Warrants paid out
budget_items.what_was_said: Staff reported a routine warrant total alongside the donations for approval.

budget_items.topic: LEAF grants (Lunenburg Education Accelerator Foundation)
budget_items.what_was_said: LEAF's first year of fundraising produced six grants to district programs (sound system/headsets, erector sets, STEM programming, a history program, and magazine subscriptions), submitted for committee acceptance.

budget_items.topic: Lunenburg Musicators donations
budget_items.what_was_said: The Musicators' president requested approval of two donations: new color guard uniforms/gloves, and funding for the middle school jazz band stipend.

budget_items.topic: Football helmets donation withdrawn
budget_items.what_was_said: The football boosters had offered to buy extra helmets, but because helmets are integral to student safety the district will cover that cost itself, so the donation was withdrawn from the packet.

budget_items.topic: Football boosters transportation donation
budget_items.what_was_said: With transportation cut from the athletic budget, the boosters proposed funding one-way bus transportation to away games for football and cheerleading, to be given in installments so the club retains starting funds.

budget_items.topic: FY26 earmark for passenger vans
budget_items.what_was_said: An FY26 state earmark to purchase 10-passenger vans for smaller programs was finalized and the vans have been ordered.

budget_items.topic: FY27 technology infrastructure earmark
budget_items.what_was_said: Senator Cronin's office secured a state earmark for FY27 designated for district technology/infrastructure upgrades; a spending plan is being developed with technology and buildings and grounds staff.

budget_items.topic: ESSA (federal) entitlement grants: Title II, Title IV, Title I
budget_items.what_was_said: Title II and Title IV allocations were relatively flat with slight decreases; Title I came in well above what the district had budgeted for, with the superintendent noting the district does not know the reason for the increase. Title II funds are earmarked for math professional development, Title IV for trauma-informed practice/school climate work, and Title I for instructional coaching aimed at struggling students.

budget_items.topic: FY27 additional state-aid warrant article amount
budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked the committee to revisit and increase the amount requested in the warrant article for the upcoming special town meeting, from the previously voted figure to the full education-related increase, or possibly the full town-wide cherry sheet increase.

budget_items.topic: Proposed use of additional funds: occupational therapy assistant position
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent proposed restoring a certified occupational therapy assistant position, tied to rising caseloads and a new state restriction on school 'cool down rooms' that arrived with no accompanying funding.

budget_items.topic: Amended warrant article amount
budget_items.what_was_said: The committee reread and formally amended the warrant article language to request the full education-related cherry sheet increase for the FY27 school operating budget, rather than the smaller amount previously voted.

budget_items.topic: Proposed millionaire's-tax per-pupil funding (state level)
budget_items.what_was_said: The governor proposed additional per-pupil funding drawn from millionaire's-tax revenue, pending legislative approval, which if passed would go directly to districts without a town meeting vote. A member cautioned the amount, even if approved, would not be enough to restore multiple cut positions.

budget_items.topic: Custodial union (AFSCME Council 93) contract terms
budget_items.what_was_said: The negotiated custodial contract includes annual salary increases over three years, two added steps, revised longevity payments now expressed as flat dollar amounts by years of service, and an increased clothing allowance.

Middle school guidance counselors to high school guidance counselors and high school guidance secretary
High school long-term substitutes to high school regular substitutes

decisions.decision: A member's citizen petition triggered a legal requirement that the select board hold a special town meeting within 45 days; the committee is treating September 3rd as that meeting, referred to informally as the 'extra special' town meeting.

The committee agreed to submit its own warrant article, taking ownership of and editing the language originally filed as a citizen petition, rather than leaving the citizen petition as the vehicle; the citizen who filed the petition said she would not separately pursue a specific dollar amount through it.

At a joint select board/municipal building design committee meeting, an informal straw poll (not a recorded vote) favored eventually taking down the TCP building, with one dissent, on the view that it has no remaining municipal use.
The athletic advisory committee is being restarted to help coordinate booster-club fundraising and ensure compliance with legal requirements on accepting donations.

No August meeting is currently planned unless needed for additional line-item transfers; the committee's next meeting is the day before the September special town meeting, with a finance committee meeting also expected before then.

minutes.summary: This School Committee meeting covered public comment urging action on the long-neglected Turkey Hill Elementary building, a detailed walkthrough of state cherry sheet aid increases, a large batch of routine year-end line-item transfers, several donations (LEAF grants, Lunenburg Musicators, football boosters), the superintendent's report on new hires and grants, and a proposal for 300th-anniversary fireworks. The committee's central business was amending its warrant article to request more of the state's additional education aid for a September 3rd special town meeting, alongside sending a legislative letter for further per-pupil funding and ratifying a new custodial union contract; an FY26 budget update was tabled for a future meeting.

Accept the new custodial union contract/MOU as ratified by AFSCME Council 93
